sections.title: Turning Actions into Pre-Nominal Attributes
sections.content: The suffix -ó (back-vowel verbs: kopog -> kopogó, suhan -> suhanó) and -ő (front-vowel verbs: gördül -> gördülő, érkezik -> érkező) creates an active present participle (folyamatos melléknévi igenév). It describes an ongoing or characteristic action performed by the modified noun.

sections.title: Expanding the Participial Phrase
sections.content: In B2 prose, the participle rarely stands alone. It keeps its own adverbials or direct objects to its left, and the entire package sits between the article 'a/az' and the head noun: 'a [macskaköveken kopogó] patkók' (the horseshoes clattering on the cobblestones).

sections.title: Expanded -ó/-ő Participial Phrases
rows: the stagecoach rolling in the autumn mist
the horseshoes clattering on the cobblestones
the wind arriving from the direction of the Danube
the breeze carrying the scent of leaves

items.spanish: Rezeda Kázmér a macskaköveken kopogó patkók hangját hallgatta.
items.english: Kázmér Rezeda listened to the sound of the horseshoes clattering on the cobblestones.

items.spanish: A Duna felől érkező szél végigsöpört a kihalt rakparton.
items.english: The wind arriving from the Danube swept along the deserted embankment.

items.spanish: A sarokban halkan játszó hegedűs régi dallamot húzott.
items.english: The violinist playing softly in the corner bowed an old melody.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: When reading a complex noun phrase starting with 'a/az', scan forward to the participle (-ó/-ő) and the noun immediately after it first—everything between the article and the participle modifies that participle!
